question: Choose the correct statement from the given options. The press is a democracy must: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: highlight the achievements of the government without criticising its policies
be committed to the policies of the government
criticise the policies of the government
be free and impartial
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is be free and impartial

Explanation:
In a democracy, the press is considered the fourth pillar of the state. Its primary role is to scrutinize government policies impartially and provide accurate information to the public. The press should highlight both achievements and failures of the government without any external pressure. It must remain free and impartial to ensure accountability and transparency in the democratic system. Press freedom is protected by the Constitution and should be free from any governmental control. Thus, the correct statement is that the press must be free and impartial.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which article guarantees press freedom in India? → Article 19(1)(a)
☛ Which pillar of democracy is the press? → Fourth pillar
☛ Principle ensuring press impartiality → Journalistic ethics
☛ When was the Press Council of India established? → 1966
☛ On what grounds can press freedom be restricted? → Under Article 19(2)
question_hi: दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही कथन का चयन कीजिए। प्रेस एक लोकतंत्र है: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/02/2021) Shift 2)

Explanation:
लोकतंत्र में प्रेस की भूमिका चौथा स्तंभ मानी जाती है। इसका मुख्य कार्य सरकार की नीतियों की निष्पक्ष जांच करना और जनता को सही जानकारी देना है। प्रेस को सरकार की उपलब्धियों के साथ-साथ कमियों को भी उजागर करना चाहिए, बिना किसी दबाव के। यह स्वतंत्र और निष्पक्ष होना चाहिए ताकि लोकतंत्र में जवाबदेही और पारदर्शिता बनी रहे। प्रेस की स्वतंत्रता संविधान द्वारा संरक्षित है और इसे किसी भी सरकारी नियंत्रण से मुक्त रहना चाहिए। इस प्रकार, सही कथन यह है कि प्रेस को स्वतंत्र और निष्पक्ष रहना चाहिए।

question: ________ describe(s) India as a secular state. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (09/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: The Preamble of the Constitution
Directive Principles of State Policy
Article 44
Article 475
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Preamble of the Constitution

Explanation:
The Preamble of the Indian Constitution describes India as a secular state. It declares India as a 'Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic'. The term 'secular' was added by the 42nd Amendment (1976). Secularism means that the state does not have an official religion and treats all religions equally. The Preamble is part of the basic structure of the Constitution. Other options like Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV), Article 44 (Uniform Civil Code), and Article 475 (which does not exist) do not describe India as a secular state like the Preamble does.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which part describes India as secular? → Preamble
☛ Which amendment added 'secular'? → 42nd Amendment
☛ How many adjectives are in Preamble? → 6 (Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic, after 42nd Amendment)
☛ Source of Preamble is? → US Constitution
☛ Meaning of secularism? → State not aligned to any religion
question_hi: ________ भारत को एक धर्मनिरपेक्ष राज्य के रूप में वर्णित करते हैं। (RRB NTPC CBT-I (09/02/2021) Shift 2)

राज्य के नीति निर्देशक सिद्धांत

अनुच्छेद 475
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है संविधान की प्रस्तावना

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान की प्रस्तावना भारत को एक धर्मनिरपेक्ष राज्य घोषित करती है। यह संविधान के मूल ढांचे का हिस्सा है और 42वें संशोधन (1976) द्वारा इसमें 'धर्मनिरपेक्ष' शब्द जोड़ा गया था। प्रस्तावना में भारत को 'संप्रभु, समाजवादी, धर्मनिरपेक्ष, लोकतांत्रिक गणराज्य' बताया गया है। धर्मनिरपेक्षता का अर्थ है कि राज्य किसी भी धर्म को आधिकारिक धर्म के रूप में नहीं मानता और सभी धर्मों को समान आदर देता है। अन्य विकल्प जैसे राज्य के नीति निर्देशक सिद्धांत (भाग-4), अनुच्छेद 44 (समान नागरिक संहिता) और अनुच्छेद 475 (जो अस्तित्व में नहीं है) प्रस्तावना की तरह भारत को धर्मनिरपेक्ष राज्य के रूप में वर्णित नहीं करते।

question: As per Constitution of India, if for a period of ________ days a member of either House of Parliament is, without permission of the House, absent from all meetings thereof, the House may declare his seat vacant. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (16/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: 60
30
45
15
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 60

Explanation:
According to Article 101(4) of the Constitution of India, if a member of either House of Parliament is absent from all meetings for a period of 60 days without the permission of the House, the House may declare his seat vacant. This provision ensures that members attend Parliament regularly and fulfill their duties. However, the House may excuse the absence if it considers the reasons satisfactory. This rule applies to both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. The period of 60 days is calculated continuously, and the House has the discretion to condone the absence in genuine cases. This helps maintain discipline among legislators.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Article providing for vacation of seat due to absence → Article 101(4)
☛ Minimum absence period for declaring seat vacant → 60 days
☛ Can the House condone absence? → Yes, if reasons are satisfactory
☛ Which Houses are covered? → Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
☛ Does this apply to state legislatures? → Yes, similar provision exists for state assemblies

question: When did an Indian chief minister hoist the national flag on Independence Day for the first time? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (16/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: 15th August 1950
15th August 1947
15th August 1977
15th August 1974
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 15th August 1974

Explanation:
The first Indian chief minister to hoist the national flag on Independence Day was M. Karunanidhi, the then Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu. This historic event took place on 15th August 1974. From 1947 to 1974, the privilege of hoisting the flag on Independence Day was reserved only for the Prime Minister or central ministers. Karunanidhi broke this tradition by hoisting the flag in Chennai, setting a new precedent for state governments. Later, in 1977, the Janata Party government allowed all chief ministers to hoist the flag on Independence Day. This event was a significant step towards strengthening Indian federalism and state autonomy.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ First CM to hoist flag on Independence Day → M. Karunanidhi (Tamil Nadu)
☛ Year → 15th August 1974
☛ Earlier flag hoisting right → Only Prime Minister
☛ Permission to all CMs → Granted in 1977 by Janata Party government
☛ Significance → Strengthened state autonomy and federalism

question: Which of the following statements is true with regard to the Election Commission of India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (01/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: It is Constituted every four years.
It is a Permanent constitutional body.
It is Constituted every six years.
It is Constituted every five years.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It is a Permanent constitutional body.

Explanation:
The Election Commission of India is a permanent constitutional body established under Article 324 of the Indian Constitution. It is not constituted periodically but continues to function indefinitely. The members are appointed by the President and hold office for a fixed term or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier. The primary role of the Election Commission is to conduct free and fair elections in the country. The other options are incorrect because the Election Commission is not constituted every four, five, or six years; it is a permanent institution that operates continuously.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner of India? → The President
☛ What is the term of office of an Election Commissioner? → 6 years or age of 65, whichever is earlier
☛ What type of body is the Election Commission? → Permanent constitutional body
☛ When was the Election Commission of India established? → 25 January 1950

question: According to Article 170, the number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of each State should not be more than _______. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (14/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: 550
500
525
475
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 500

Explanation:
Article 170 of the Indian Constitution deals with the composition of Legislative Assemblies of States. It states that the maximum number of members in a State Legislative Assembly shall not be more than 500, and the minimum shall not be less than 60. This provision ensures proportional representation based on population. However, some smaller states like Goa and Sikkim have been granted exceptions to the minimum limit. It is important to note that this differs from the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha, which is 550. Elections to the State Legislative Assemblies are conducted through direct voting by the people. This article is crucial for understanding the structure of state governments in India.

☛ Minimum seats in State Legislative Assembly → 60

☛ Election to State Legislative Assembly → By direct voting
question_hi: अनुच्छेद 170 के अनुसार, प्रत्येक राज्य की विधान सभा में सीटों की संख्या _______ से अधिक नहीं होनी चाहिए। (RRB NTPC CBT-I (14/03/2021) Shift 1)

question: As per the Constitution of India, who does NOT form the Council of Ministers?  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (24/07/2021) Shift 1)

Ministers of local government
solution:

Explanation:

question: The Parliament does not have the power to legislate on the subject in List 2 of the Seventh Schedule. Which of the following is an EXCEPTION in this general law?  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (24/07/2021) Shift 1)
options: If the Prime Minister asks the Parliament to do so
If the Judiciary asks the Parliament to do so
if the Governor of the state certifies the requirement
If the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution to this effect
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is If the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution to this effect

Explanation:
Under Article 249 of the Indian Constitution, if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a two-thirds majority that it is necessary in the national interest for Parliament to legislate on a matter in the State List, then Parliament can do so. This resolution remains valid for a maximum of one year and can be renewed repeatedly. Other options: The Prime Minister's or Judiciary's request does not have constitutional backing. The Governor's certificate is only effective during President's Rule under Article 356. Thus, the Rajya Sabha resolution is the correct exception to the general rule that Parliament cannot legislate on State List subjects.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India guarantees the protection of certain rights regarding the freedom of speech? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (26/07/2021) Shift 1)
options: Article 14
Article 22
Article 21
Article 19
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 19

Explanation:
Article 19 of the Indian Constitution guarantees six fundamental rights, including freedom of speech (Article 19(1)(a)). It also allows the state to impose reasonable restrictions on these rights for reasons such as security of the state, foreign relations, public order, decency, or morality. Article 19 specifically protects certain rights regarding freedom of speech, such as expression, peaceful assembly, forming associations, movement, residence, and profession. Article 14 deals with equality, Article 21 with right to life, and Article 22 with protection against arrest.

question: Money bill can be introduced _________. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (31/07/2021) Shift 2)
options: by neither Lok Sabha nor Rajya Sabha
only in Lok Sabha
only in Rajya Sabha
by either house of Parliament
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is only in Lok Sabha

Explanation:
According to Article 109 of the Indian Constitution, a Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha. The Rajya Sabha has no power to reject or amend a Money Bill; it can only make recommendations within 14 days. If the Rajya Sabha fails to act within 14 days, the bill is deemed passed in the form as passed by the Lok Sabha. The definition of a Money Bill is given in Article 110, covering matters such as taxation, government expenditure, borrowing public money, etc. The prior recommendation of the President is required for introducing a Money Bill in the Lok Sabha.

question: Which of the following is not the original Fundamental Duty?  (RPF SI 2018 (13/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Protecting the Country's Rich Heritage
Protecting Public Property
Right to Constitutional Remedies
Development of Scientific Thinking, Humanity and Curiosity
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Right to Constitutional Remedies

Explanation:
The Fundamental Duties are enshrined in Part IV-A, Article 51A of the Indian Constitution. Originally, 10 duties were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, including protecting the country's rich heritage, protecting public property, and developing scientific thinking and humanity. The Right to Constitutional Remedies under Article 32 is a Fundamental Right, not a duty. The 11th duty was added by the 86th Amendment in 2002, requiring parents to provide education opportunities to children aged 6-14 years. Thus, the Right to Constitutional Remedies is not an original Fundamental Duty.

question: How many times has the National Emergency been implemented in India? (RPF SI 2018 (13/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Never
Three times
Twice
Only once
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Three times

Explanation:
Under Article 352 of the Indian Constitution, a National Emergency can be proclaimed. India has imposed a National Emergency three times so far. The first was on 26 October 1962 during the India-China war, the second on 3 December 1971 during the India-Pakistan war, and the third on 25 June 1975 on grounds of internal disturbance. The 1975 Emergency, imposed by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, was the most controversial and lasted until 1977. No National Emergency has been imposed in India since the third one.

question: What does the word 'sine die' mean in the context of indefinite postponement? (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: For two hours
For half day
For Indefinitely
For one hour
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is For Indefinitely

Explanation:
'Sine die' is a Latin term meaning 'without a day fixed'. It is used in parliamentary proceedings to adjourn a meeting or session indefinitely. When a house is adjourned 'sine die', it means the house is postponed without setting a date for the next meeting, effectively suspending it until the next session. This differs from a regular adjournment, where the next meeting date is specified. In the Indian Parliament, adjourning the Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha 'sine die' implies that the house is adjourned until the next session. The term is commonly used in legislative bodies and legal contexts to indicate an indefinite postponement.

question: Which of these is a new feature of Indian Constitution? (RPF SI 2018 (11/01/2019) Shift 3)

question: Which amendment converted the right to property from a fundamental right to a simple legal right under article 300A? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (07/04/2021) Shift 2)
options: 44th Amendment
46th Amendment
42nd Amendment
40th Amendment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 44th Amendment

Explanation:
The 44th Amendment (1978) of the Indian Constitution removed the right to property from being a fundamental right under Article 31 and made it a simple legal right under Article 300A. This amendment was passed by the Morarji Desai government. Article 31 was repealed, and the right to property is now regulated only by law. The change aimed to facilitate land reforms and socialist policies. According to Article 300A, no person shall be deprived of his property except by authority of law. Although it is no longer justiciable as a fundamental right, constitutional remedies are still available. The 44th Amendment also introduced other changes, such as abridging the power to declare a national emergency.

अनुच्छेद 32-52
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 36-51

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के भाग IV में राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्वों (DPSP) का प्रावधान है। ये तत्व अनुच्छेद 36 से 51 तक विस्तृत हैं। ये तत्व राज्य को नीतियाँ बनाने में मार्गदर्शन प्रदान करते हैं, हालांकि ये न्यायोचित नहीं हैं। DPSP का उद्देश्य सामाजिक-आर्थिक लोकतंत्र स्थापित करना और कल्याणकारी राज्य की अवधारणा को लागू करना है। अनुच्छेद 36 'राज्य' की परिभाषा देता है, जबकि अनुच्छेद 51 अंतर्राष्ट्रीय शांति और सुरक्षा से संबंधित है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि मौलिक अधिकार अनुच्छेद 12-35 में हैं, जबकि DPSP अनुच्छेद 36-51 में।
